name: W identity
summary: A W-spider with a single output is the identity wire.
description:
The W-spider (black triangle) with one input and $n$ outputs maps $|0\rangle \mapsto |0\cdots 0\rangle$ and $|1\rangle \mapsto |10\cdots0\rangle + |010\cdots0\rangle + \cdots + |0\cdots01\rangle$: it spreads a single excitation over its outputs in all possible ways. The small dot marks its input leg. With just one output it maps $|0\rangle\mapsto|0\rangle$ and $|1\rangle\mapsto|1\rangle$, so it is the identity.

In the undirected ZW-calculus, the binary black vertex is the NOT gate $|01\rangle+|10\rangle$, and PyZX's W-spider with one output consists of two such vertices in a row. The rule is then axiom 2a of Hadzihasanovic: the binary black vertex is an involution.

also_in.location: Chapter 5, Section 5.2 (list of rules of the ZW calculus), rule $inv$
